summary: Back on the Galilean shore, Jesus refuses the Pharisees’ and Sadducees’ demand for a sign from heaven and points them to the sign of Jonah.
key_insight: The demand came straight after Jesus had fed four thousand and healed many. The leaders did not lack evidence; they wanted a sign on their own terms. Mark records that Jesus “sighed deeply in His spirit.”
story: Jesus sent the crowd away, got into the boat with His disciples, and came to the region of Magdala. {Mt} Mark names the place Dalmanutha. {Mk}
Then the Pharisees came out and began to dispute with Him. {Mk} Sadducees came with them, {Mt} and to test Him they asked Him to show them a sign from heaven.

Jesus sighed deeply in His spirit. {Mk} He answered, “When it is evening you say, ‘It will be fair weather, for the sky is red’; and in the morning, ‘It will be foul weather today, for the sky is red and threatening.’ Hypocrites! You know how to discern the face of the sky, but you cannot discern the signs of the times.” {Mt}

“Why does this generation seek a sign?” He asked. {Mk} “A wicked and adulterous generation seeks after a sign, and no sign shall be given to it except the sign of the prophet Jonah.” {Mt} And He left them and departed.
differences: Matthew calls the place Magdala; Mark calls it Dalmanutha.
Matthew says the Pharisees came with Sadducees; Mark mentions only the Pharisees.
Only Matthew records the saying about the red sky and “the signs of the times”; only Mark says Jesus “sighed deeply in His spirit.”
In Mark, Jesus says no sign will be given to this generation; in Matthew He adds “except the sign of the prophet Jonah.”

fit.question: Mark says “no sign shall be given to this generation.” Matthew says no sign “except the sign of the prophet Jonah.” Did Jesus refuse a sign or promise one?

points.label: No sign on demand
points.text: Jesus refused the kind of sign they asked for: a proof from the sky, performed at their command. Mark records that refusal plainly.

points.label: The sign God would give
points.text: Matthew adds the exception Jesus had already named in Matthew 12:39–40: as Jonah was three days in the great fish, the Son of Man would be three days in the heart of the earth. That sign was not theirs to order. God would give it in the resurrection.

fit.note: Mark gives the refusal and Matthew gives the exception; together they show a Jesus who would not perform for skeptics but would rise from the dead.
fit.short: Jesus refused a sign on demand (Mark). Matthew adds the one exception, the sign of Jonah: His death and resurrection.

fit.question: Matthew says they came to Magdala; Mark says Dalmanutha. Which was it?

points.label: Two names for one district
points.text: Dalmanutha is not mentioned anywhere else in ancient writings. It was most likely a village or landing place near Magdala, so the two names point to the same stretch of shore.

points.label: Uncertain names
points.text: Some manuscripts of Matthew read Magadan instead of Magdala. Neither Magadan nor Dalmanutha has been located for certain, so the exact spot cannot be fixed.

fit.note: The difficulty lies in our maps of ancient Galilee, not in the Gospels; both writers place Jesus on the same shore.
fit.short: Dalmanutha was probably a village or landing place near Magdala. The two writers name the same district differently.

scene.label: Magdala
scene.text: A fishing town on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, a few miles north of Tiberias, and probably the hometown of Mary Magdalene. Crossing the lake brought Jesus out of the Decapolis and back among Jewish towns.

scene.label: Unlikely allies
scene.text: Pharisees and Sadducees seldom agreed. The Pharisees held to the traditions of the elders; the Sadducees, many of them from priestly families, rejected those traditions and denied the resurrection (Acts 23:8). Here they join to test Jesus.

scene.label: A sign from heaven
scene.text: Jesus had healed and fed thousands. His opponents wanted something else: a sign from the sky, the kind of proof they thought only God could give, like the fire that fell at Elijah’s prayer (1 Kings 18:38).

scene.label: A red sky
scene.text: Jesus quotes common weather lore that fishermen and farmers lived by. They could read tomorrow’s weather in the clouds but not what God was doing in front of them.

witnesses.matthew: Records the weather saying and the sign of Jonah, tying this scene to Jesus’ earlier answer in Matthew 12:39–40. Matthew alone names the Sadducees here, and a few verses later Jesus warns against the teaching of both parties (Matthew 16:12).
witnesses.mark: Keeps the scene short and lets one detail carry it: Jesus “sighed deeply in His spirit.” Mark records the refusal without the exception, so the scene ends with Jesus leaving His questioners behind.

seeing.reveals: Jesus will not perform on demand. He grieves over hearts that want proof on their own terms, and He points them to the one sign God would give: His death and rising.
seeing.living: These men stood face to face with Jesus and still asked for evidence. Do not set terms for God to meet before you trust Him. Look to the risen Christ, the sign He has already given.
seeing.ponder: What proof have you been waiting for before you fully trust Jesus, and what has He already shown you?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus refuses signs on demand and offers the one sign that matters: His resurrection.
preaching.watch_for: Matthew records this answer twice (12:39 and 16:4). The repetition shows a pattern: unbelief keeps asking for proof, and Jesus keeps pointing to His resurrection.
